messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 99th latency on /v1/streaming in us-west-2. Queue depth rising, streaming sessions long-lived. Pager routed to on-call (Liam). Dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood/graph?panel=streaming_tail

Liam: taking this — on-call for eng-sre. I'll triage now.

Alex: I see the backlog in the streaming router logs. Non-streaming endpoints look normal. Suspect long-lived connections blocking batching and causing token stalls.

Jamie: are GPUs pegged or is it connection count?

Alex: some GPUs ~90% but qps is steady. Lots of open SSE connections holding KV caches alive; batching effectiveness dropped.

Priya: any immediate customer impact? Which tenants are hitting this?

Maria: quick trace: ~8-15% of requests are streaming in last 10m. Error rate for streaming went from 0.2% -> 3.5%. Top affected customers: AcmeCorp, DataWave. I've opened CS ticket and flagged high-touch accounts.

Liam: mitigation proposal: 1) Flip streaming feature flag to disable streaming responses (global) 2) If needed, apply per-tenant soft rate caps for streaming 3) Monitor latency/throughput, then re-enable staged once stable. Goal: stabilize 99th latency within 15m.

Alex: I can do a canary disable to 10% first via Console API. Command (canary):
```bash
POST https://console.internal/api/flags/streaming
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "canary": 10,
  "reason": "emergency-mitigation"
}
```

DeployBot: Feature flag update initiated -> rollout id ff-2026-1945 (canary 10%).

Alex: Canary metrics: canary group 99th latency down ~30%, queue depth reduced on canary nodes. CPU headroom freed.

Liam: proceed to 100% if canary looks good. Keep on-call handoff notes.

Alex: promoting rollout to 100% now.

Alex: Command (promote): `POST https://console.internal/api/flags/streaming/rollout -d '{"percent":100}'`

DeployBot: Rollout to 100% complete. ff-2026-1945 status: success.

Jamie: seeing overall 99th latency drop back to baseline within 3m. Queue depth trending down across the cluster.

Priya: need a customer communications note. Maria, can you coordinate with CS?

Maria: drafted message in CS tracker: "We're temporarily suspending streaming responses to stabilize latency. Polling/fallback will continue to work. We expect restoration once metrics are healthy." Sending to AcmeCorp + support inbox now.

Liam: also applied temporary soft cap at the ingress for streaming endpoints before the flag flip (20rps per-tenant) to reduce new long-lived sessions.

Alex: details of changes applied to incident timeline:
```bash
# canary disable
curl -X POST 'https://console.internal/api/flags/streaming' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -d '{"enabled":false,"canary":10}'
# promote to 100%
curl -X POST 'https://console.internal/api/flags/streaming/rollout' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -d '{"percent":100}'
# apply soft rate limit
kubectl -n inference patch configmap rate-limits --patch '{"data":{"streaming":"20"}}'
```

DeployBot: Rate-limit patch applied to ingress configmap.

Jamie: I'll own the primary watch for the next 45m, Liam please standby for escalation. I'll update status every 10m.

Liam: noted. I'll monitor dashboards and alerting; ready to scale GPUs if we see unexpected regressions. Suggested next step if toggle insufficient: add +2 GPU nodes and reduce max batch size.

IncidentBot: Incident declared SEV-2. Channel created: #incidents. Postmortem requested if service not fully stable within 2 hours.

Alex: Recording mitigation steps and timeline in incident ticket: https://issues.internal/RED-1234.

Priya: thanks all. Quick ask from Support: confirm whether token usage or billing changes while streaming is suspended.

Maria: billing unaffected; token counting continues for non-streaming calls. Notifying finance and support with copy.

Jamie: after 30 minutes metrics stabilized (99th latency at baseline, error rate back down). Plan: hold streaming off for a full 60m of stable metrics, then staged re-enable (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with metric gates.

Liam: ack. I'll remain on standby for the re-enable window.

Alex: adding follow-up items: run query to find long-lived session causes (client-side keep-alive patterns or backend idle timeout), evaluate batching heuristics.

Maria: CS outreach completed for affected accounts.

Jamie: closing mitigation update — latency stabilized, no additional mitigations required. Creating post-incident action items.

Liam: great work. Summary: streaming temporarily suspended, rate caps applied, metrics returned to normal. Postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
